body:
# obsidian

a sourced history of obsidian, its people, the discourse around it, and the file-over-app idea it is built on.

obsidian answered the tools-for-thought wave the opposite way roam did: local files, no venture capital, and a plugin community as the moat. this is the record of how that bet worked — the dynalist origin, the people who built it, the side quests around it, the coverage, and why plain files might be the best substrate agents ever got.

- [history](https://hraness.com/obsidian/history): the company, sourced and dated — dynalist, the 2020 beta, and building in public without vc.
  - [the dynalist years](https://hraness.com/obsidian/history#dynalist): shida li and erica xu build the outliner that becomes obsidian's runway.
  - [the beta](https://hraness.com/obsidian/history#beta): the early-2020 beta, the discord community, and launch into lockdown.
  - [building in public](https://hraness.com/obsidian/history#building): sync, publish, catalyst, mobile, 1.0 — the business model takes shape in public.
  - [the kepano era](https://hraness.com/obsidian/history#kepano): the minimal theme author joins, then becomes ceo — and the philosophy gets a public voice.
  - [recent history](https://hraness.com/obsidian/history#recent): canvas, web clipper, bases — the product keeps compounding while the industry pivots to ai.
- [people](https://hraness.com/obsidian/people): shida li, erica xu, and steph ango — who they are, what they wrote, and what they believe.
  - [the founders](https://hraness.com/obsidian/people#founders): shida li and erica xu — the private founders behind dynalist and obsidian.
  - [the ceo who writes](https://hraness.com/obsidian/people#kepano): steph ango's essay corpus — file over app, paying for software, and calm technology.
  - [the team](https://hraness.com/obsidian/people#team): liam cain, johannes theiner, rebbecca bishop — the small staff behind the small company.
  - [interviews and talks](https://hraness.com/obsidian/people#appearances): interviews, podcasts, and talks where the philosophy got said out loud.
  - [the philosophy](https://hraness.com/obsidian/people#philosophy): ownership, longevity, privacy, and software that respects its user.
- [side quests](https://hraness.com/obsidian/side-quests): the pursuits around the company — minimal, flexoki, inkodye and lumi, dynalist, minecraft plugins, and the ecosystem's own projects.
  - [kepano's quests](https://hraness.com/obsidian/side-quests#kepano-quests): minimal, flexoki, defuddle, inkodye, lumi, and the rest of steph ango's orbit.
  - [the founders' quests](https://hraness.com/obsidian/side-quests#founder-quests): what shida li and erica xu built and wrote outside obsidian.
  - [the ecosystem's quests](https://hraness.com/obsidian/side-quests#ecosystem): obsidian october, community talks, and the plugin economy as its own scene.
- [coverage](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage): what the discourse made of obsidian — the darling phase, the canonization, and the critiques.
  - [the breakout](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage#breakout): the 2020–2021 arrival: hacker news threads, influencer waves, and the underdog story.
  - [the canonization](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage#canon): wirecutter picks, mainstream profiles, and the tool-for-thought canonization.
  - [the critiques](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage#critique): closed source, plugin security, pricing debates, and the productivity-porn charge.
  - [the comparisons](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage#comparisons): obsidian vs notion, roam, logseq, tana — the genre that defined it by opposition.
  - [the departures](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage#departures): the leaving-obsidian genre — notebooklm, capacities, plain folders, and the confessions.
  - [controversies](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage#controversies): closed source, no sandbox, pricing, phantompulse — the ten running debates.
  - [sentiment eras](https://hraness.com/obsidian/coverage#eras): sentiment phases from underdog to institution, with the evidence for each.
- [the idea](https://hraness.com/obsidian/the-idea): file over app — the lineage obsidian inherited, what it proved, and what agents do to it.
  - [lineage](https://hraness.com/obsidian/the-idea#lineage): memex to zettelkasten to local-first — the fork obsidian took from roam's line.
  - [what obsidian proved](https://hraness.com/obsidian/the-idea#proved): what the local-files bet actually demonstrated at scale.
  - [what stayed unfinished](https://hraness.com/obsidian/the-idea#stalled): collaboration, capture friction, and the honest ledger of what never landed.
  - [the agent-era turn](https://hraness.com/obsidian/the-idea#agent-era): plain markdown on disk as the best substrate an agent could ask for.
  - [successors](https://hraness.com/obsidian/the-idea#successors): wordcell, sponge, oh, and the projects carrying file-over-app into the agent world.
  - [open questions](https://hraness.com/obsidian/the-idea#open-questions): the questions a next attempt has to answer.
- [sources](https://hraness.com/obsidian/sources): every source cited in the obsidian history, with its date and type.
  - [the catalog](https://hraness.com/obsidian/sources#catalog): the full typed catalog — primary, interview, reporting, archive, community.
- [method](https://hraness.com/obsidian/method): how ai agents researched the obsidian history, the evidence rules they followed, and what they could not verify.
  - [the lanes](https://hraness.com/obsidian/method#lanes): the four parallel research lanes and what the formula proved.
  - [the evidence rules](https://hraness.com/obsidian/method#rules): the evidence model — confidence, precision, sentiment discipline.
  - [known gaps](https://hraness.com/obsidian/method#gaps): what the research could not verify — recorded, not hidden.
  - [corrections](https://hraness.com/obsidian/method#corrections): how to correct the record.

AI-drafted at Ben Guo's direct request and credited to Hraness; every claim links to its cataloged source.

Canonical page: https://hraness.com/obsidian
